claims.claim: Civil Code §1788.17 requires every collector collecting or attempting to collect a California consumer debt to comply with 15 U.S.C. §§1692b–1692j.
claims.quote: every debt collector collecting or attempting to collect a consumer debt shall comply with the provisions of Sections 1692b to 1692j, inclusive, of, and shall be subject to the remedies in Section 1692k of, Title 15 of the United States Code.
claims.note: The range is correct, but California incorporates the federal text as of January 1, 2001. The draft also omits the §1692e(11) exception.

claims.claim: Section 1692g does not apply under §1788.17 to the persons specified in §1692a(6)(A) and (B) or their principal.
claims.quote: However, subsection (11) of Section 1692e and Section 1692g shall not apply to any person specified in paragraphs (A) and (B) of subsection (6) of Section 1692a of Title 15 of the United States Code or that person’s principal.

claims.claim: The supplied federal rules, including §1692g(d), apply as stated through California's incorporation of §1692g.
claims.note: This linkage is implied by the draft. The January 1, 2001 federal text needed to check it was not provided; the supplied federal edition lists a later amendment.

claims.claim: Under federal §1692g(a), the collector must send the consumer a written notice within five days after the initial collection communication.
claims.quote: Within five days after the initial communication with a consumer in connection with the collection of any debt, a debt collector shall, unless the following information is contained in the initial communication or the consumer has paid the debt, send the consumer a written notice containing—
claims.note: Subject to the two exceptions stated in the draft.

claims.claim: No separate notice is required if the initial communication contains the required information.
claims.quote: unless the following information is contained in the initial communication or the consumer has paid the debt

claims.claim: No separate notice is required if the consumer has paid the debt.
claims.quote: or the consumer has paid the debt

claims.claim: The notice must give the amount of the debt.
The notice must name the creditor.
claims.quote: (2) the name of the creditor to whom the debt is owed;

claims.claim: The notice must say the debt will be assumed valid unless disputed within thirty days after receipt.
claims.quote: (3) a statement that unless the consumer, within thirty days after receipt of the notice, disputes the validity of the debt, or any portion thereof, the debt will be assumed to be valid by the debt collector;
claims.note: The deadline is correct. The assumption is the collector's, and the consumer can dispute just a portion.

claims.claim: The notice must say the collector will obtain verification if the consumer disputes the debt in writing within that period.
claims.quote: if the consumer notifies the debt collector in writing within the thirty-day period that the debt, or any portion thereof, is disputed, the debt collector will obtain verification of the debt or a copy of a judgment against the consumer and a copy of such verification or judgment will be mailed to the consumer by the debt collector
claims.note: The consumer must notify the collector. The notice also covers partial disputes, the judgment alternative, and mailing a copy to the consumer.

claims.claim: The notice must promise the original creditor's name and address on written request within the thirty-day period.
claims.quote: upon the consumer's written request within the thirty-day period, the debt collector will provide the consumer with the name and address of the original creditor, if different from the current creditor.
claims.note: The draft omits “if different from the current creditor.”

claims.claim: A written dispute within thirty days requires the collector to stop collecting the disputed debt.
claims.quote: If the consumer notifies the debt collector in writing within the thirty-day period described in subsection (a) that the debt, or any portion thereof, is disputed, or that the consumer requests the name and address of the original creditor, the debt collector shall cease collection of the debt, or any disputed portion thereof,
claims.note: The collector must be notified. If only part is disputed, the stop applies to that portion. A timely written original-creditor request is a separate trigger.

claims.claim: The dispute-triggered stop lasts until the collector mails verification.
claims.quote: until the debt collector obtains verification of the debt or a copy of a judgment, or the name and address of the original creditor, and a copy of such verification or judgment, or name and address of the original creditor, is mailed to the consumer by the debt collector.
claims.note: For a dispute, a judgment copy is an alternative to verification; the mailing must be to the consumer.

claims.claim: A court may not treat failure to dispute under §1692g as an admission of liability.
claims.quote: The failure of a consumer to dispute the validity of a debt under this section may not be construed by any court as an admission of liability by the consumer.

claims.claim: A formal pleading in a civil action is not an initial communication.
claims.quote: A communication in the form of a formal pleading in a civil action shall not be treated as an initial communication for purposes of subsection (a).
claims.note: The exclusion is expressly limited to subsection (a).

flags.text: Section 1788.17 says: “The references to federal codes in this section refer to those codes as they read January 1, 2001.” The 2024 federal edition alone cannot establish the incorporated rules.
The blanket California compliance statement omits the §1692e(11) exception for the same persons and principals exempted from §1692g.
“The debt will be assumed valid” could be read as a court consequence of silence. Only the collector's assumption is specified; a consumer may also dispute only part of the debt.

The draft omits that a timely written request for original-creditor information also stops collection. Otherwise permissible collection can continue during the thirty days absent a qualifying notice and must not overshadow the disclosed rights.
Verification is not the only dispute response, original-creditor disclosure is conditional, and the formal-pleading exclusion is specific to the subsection (a) notice trigger.

result.summary: The supplied federal text supports the five-day deadline, its two exceptions, the thirty-day clock from receipt, and the non-admission rule. Several notice and collection-stop conditions are missing, and the federal text incorporated by California was not supplied.
